lines.trans: Nastya and I are already sitting down at the table, bring the ring.
Sveta, did you already find the keys in my jacket?
Tell me, did you not touch anything else in the pocket there?
Forgive me, darling, I simply could not help myself!
The ring is simply wonderful, and of course I agree!
I understand that the odds on their defeat are very high.
But I am completely sure that they will win today, bet everything!
Viktor, tell me, what is going on with our staff today?
All day they have been telling the guests some strange truth!
Wait, are you completely sure that they are telling the truth?
Chef, excuse me, should we save pasta for your lunch?
It is just that all the staff in the hotel have already eaten!

examples.text: Сеня, а ты на работу сегодня не опаздываешь?
examples.trans: Senya, are you not late for work today?

examples.text: Тимур, привет, мне сегодня срочно нужна белладонна.
examples.trans: Timur, hi, I urgently need belladonna today.

examples.text: Ладно, договорились, я сегодня вечером туда заеду.
examples.trans: Alright, deal, I will stop by there this evening.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'играть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to win', paired with 'выигрывать'.

examples.text: Поздравляем, вы выиграли большую скидку пятьдесят процентов.
examples.trans: Congratulations, you won a big fifty-percent discount.

examples.text: Говорят, что я выиграл большую скидку на кольца.
examples.trans: They say that I won a big discount on rings.

examples.text: Но я точно уверен, что они сегодня выиграют, ставь всё!
examples.trans: But I am completely sure that they will win today, bet everything!

meanings.en: to put, to place in an upright position
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тавить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'put, place', paired with 'поставить'.

examples.text: Может, подскажете строго между нами, на кого ставить?
examples.trans: Maybe you could give a hint strictly between us on whom to bet?

examples.text: Ну что, Миша, ты сегодня ставишь со мной?
examples.trans: Well what, Misha, are you betting with me today?

examples.text: Повара, скажите, кто поставил такой сильный режим в печи?
examples.trans: Chefs, tell me, who set such a strong mode on the oven?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Расскажи, как вы с Денисом, всё серьёзно?
examples.trans: Tell me, how are things with you and Denis, is it serious?

examples.text: Я очень надеюсь, что у нас всё серьёзно.
examples.trans: I really hope that everything is serious between us.

examples.text: Да, конечно, тогда всё точно будет хорошо!
examples.trans: Yes, of course, then everything will definitely be fine!

meanings.en: to go on, be happening (usually of chaos or strange events)
meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is going on, is happening'.

examples.text: Такое в стране творится!
examples.trans: So much is going on in the country!

examples.text: А, точно. Перепутал. Такое в стране творится! Продолжаем операцию.
examples.trans: Oh, right. I mixed them up. So much is going on in the country! Continue the operation.

examples.text: Такое в стране творится! Продолжаем операцию.
examples.trans: So much is going on in the country! Continue the operation.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'our', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Если нашла хорошего парня, надо сразу женить.
examples.trans: If you found a good guy, you need to marry him right away.

examples.text: Хорошо, сынок, давай забудем наши старые обиды.
examples.trans: Alright, son, let us forget our old grievances.

examples.text: Добрый день, Денис, вас приветствует наш ювелирный магазин.
examples.trans: Good afternoon, Denis, our jewelry store welcomes you.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'staff, personnel' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Виктор, скажи, что сегодня творится с нашим персоналом?
examples.trans: Viktor, tell me, what is going on with our staff today?

examples.text: Это вкусный обед для персонала.
examples.trans: This is a delicious lunch for the staff.

examples.text: Сегодня обед для персонала готовит наш огузок.
examples.trans: Today our runt is cooking lunch for the staff.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Поздравляю тебя, невеста, Денис только что купил кольцо!
examples.trans: Congratulations to you, bride, Denis just bought the ring!

examples.text: Они весь день говорят гостям какую-то странную правду!
examples.trans: All day they have been telling the guests some strange truth!

examples.text: Всё нормально.
examples.trans: Everything's fine.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'day' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Расскажи, как вы с Денисом, всё серьёзно?
examples.trans: Tell me, how are things with you and Denis, is it serious?

examples.text: Да, мы с Денисом неплохо звучим вместе.
examples.trans: Yes, Denis and I sound pretty good together.

examples.text: Добрый день, Денис, вас приветствует наш ювелирный магазин.
examples.trans: Good afternoon, Denis, our jewelry store welcomes you.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'say, speak', paired with 'сказать'.

examples.text: А не слишком ли рано об этом говорить?
examples.trans: Is it not too early to talk about that?

examples.text: Врач говорит, что у меня небольшая трещина.
examples.trans: The doctor says that I have a small fracture.

examples.text: Врач правильно говорит, за ней нужен хороший уход.
examples.trans: The doctor says rightly, she needs good care.

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common masculine noun meaning 'guests' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Шеф, там пришёл гость на бесплатный обед от шефа.
examples.trans: Chef, a guest arrived there for a free lunch from the chef.

examples.text: Давай, иди, а я пока приготовлю суп для гостя!
examples.trans: Go ahead, go, and meanwhile I will prepare soup for the guest!

examples.text: Уважаемые гости, лучше не берите этот дорогой номер.
examples.trans: Dear guests, you had better not take this expensive room.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'some kind of, some', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Бред какой-то.
examples.trans: What nonsense.

examples.text: Тебе звонил какой-то человек.
examples.trans: Some man called you.

examples.text: Бред какой-то. Но, с другой стороны, чем я рискую?
examples.trans: What nonsense. But on the other hand, what have I got to lose?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'транный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('strange, odd').

examples.text: Они весь день говорят гостям какую-то странную правду!
examples.trans: All day they have been telling the guests some strange truth!

examples.text: Она совсем странная.
examples.trans: She's really strange.

examples.text: Какой странный человек!
examples.trans: What a strange man!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'truth' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Врач правильно говорит, за ней нужен хороший уход.
examples.trans: The doctor says rightly, she needs good care.

examples.text: В основе сыворотки правды лежит экстракт белладонны.
examples.trans: At the base of the truth serum lies belladonna extract.

examples.text: Смотри, это настоящая сыворотка правды для того букмекера.
examples.trans: Look, this is a real truth serum for that bookmaker.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'wait', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.text: Подожди, я сейчас.
examples.trans: Wait, I'll be right there.

examples.text: Подождите минуту.
examples.trans: Wait a minute.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'винить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'excuse me', paired with 'извинять'.

examples.text: Извините, я случайно услышал, вы настоящий букмекер?
examples.trans: Excuse me, I overheard by chance, are you a real bookmaker?

examples.text: Извините, но я не понимаю, о чём вы.
examples.trans: Excuse me, but I do not understand what you mean.

examples.text: Я хотел бы заранее извиниться за нашего шефа.
examples.trans: I would like to apologize in advance for our chef.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Расскажи, как вы с Денисом, всё серьёзно?
examples.trans: Tell me, how are things with you and Denis, is it serious?

examples.text: Чего надеяться, вы отлично друг другу подходите.
examples.trans: Why just hope, you two suit each other great.

examples.text: Выбирай прямо сейчас: или она, или я!
examples.trans: Choose right now: either her or me!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'pasta' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Народ, на обед сегодня всеми любимые макароны по-флотски!
examples.trans: Folks, for lunch today is everyone's favorite navy-style pasta!

examples.text: Ребята, а вы почему макароны по-флотски не едите?
examples.trans: Guys, why are you not eating the navy-style pasta?

examples.text: А я заберу все остатки макарон себе домой.
examples.trans: And I will take all the leftover pasta home for myself.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'lunch' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Нет, я не пью, особенно с незнакомыми людьми.
examples.trans: No, I do not drink, especially with strangers.

examples.text: Ничего я не скажу, выпейте пока обезболивающее.
examples.trans: I will not say anything, drink a painkiller for now.

examples.text: Шеф, там пришёл гость на бесплатный обед от шефа.
examples.trans: Chef, a guest arrived there for a free lunch from the chef.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to leave, let someone keep', paired with 'оставить'.

examples.text: Шеф, извините, а вам макароны на обед оставлять?
examples.trans: Chef, excuse me, should we save pasta for your lunch?

examples.text: Я тебе оставляю пять миллионов.
examples.trans: I'll leave you five million.

examples.text: Не оставляй меня здесь.
examples.trans: Don't leave me here.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'отрудник'). Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'employees' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Просто все сотрудники в отеле уже давно поели!
examples.trans: It is just that all the staff in the hotel have already eaten!

examples.text: Неужели все сотрудники уже поели?
examples.trans: Did all the staff really eat already?

examples.text: Сотрудники службы начали расследование.
examples.trans: Service operatives began the investigation.

meanings.note: Agent/instrument noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-тель' ('-er'). Common masculine noun meaning 'hotel' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я хотел бы заранее извиниться за нашего шефа.
examples.trans: I would like to apologize in advance for our chef.

examples.text: Просто все сотрудники в отеле уже давно поели!
examples.trans: It is just that all the staff in the hotel have already eaten!

examples.text: Потому что я очень хотел, чтобы ты сегодня проигрался.
examples.trans: Because I really wanted you to lose your money today.

давно.gloss: for a long time; long ago

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Мама, давай сейчас же забудем все старые обиды.
examples.trans: Mom, let us forget all old grievances right now.

examples.text: Хорошо, сынок, давай забудем наши старые обиды.
examples.trans: Alright, son, let us forget our old grievances.

examples.text: Давай забудем все старые обиды.
examples.trans: Let us forget all old grievances.

поесть.gloss: to eat, to have a meal

meanings.en: to eat, to have something to eat
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'есть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to eat, to have a meal', paired with 'есть'.

examples.text: Мы только поедим.
examples.trans: We'll only eat.

examples.text: Ты уже поел сегодня?
examples.trans: Have you eaten today already?

examples.text: Ну ладно, брось! Мы только поедим.
examples.trans: Oh come on, stop it! We'll only eat.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'ужели').

examples.text: Неужели ты провёл ночь вместе со Светой?
examples.trans: Did you really spend the night together with Sveta?

examples.text: Виктор, неужели эта твоя сыворотка действительно работает?
examples.trans: Viktor, does this serum of yours really work?

examples.text: Где Лёва, неужели он опять всё блюдо испортил?
examples.trans: Where is Lyova, did he really ruin the whole dish again?
